guard: injected-wait occupancy, not wall-clock vs count×RTT, is the concurrency invariant
why: elapsed < count × inject flakes on this host: 15ms × N is smaller than per-request overhead, so a
concurrent resolve can still observe wall ABOVE serial inject. Occupancy of the synthetic waits
excludes that host work. A 15ms inject is also shorter than start stagger, so occupancy is proven
on the 160ms WAN-profile inject, where overlapped waits collapse and serialized waits sum.
M1 accounts each wait as serial delayMs instead of the union of open wait intervals. The WAN-profile
occupancy cell goes red; max-in-flight and dedupe cells stay green.
